circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, the Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke that has served as the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. As the second Middle Eastern Formula One circuit to be constructed, it followed Bahrain's establishment and preceded the later additions of Qatar and Saudi Arabia to the championship calendar.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside supporting categories including the Supercars Championship event. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 licence for motorsport competition.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: The 4. 326 km circuit located in Spielberg, Austria, was originally known as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following modifications and a rebranding to the A1-Ring, the track resumed hosting the race from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital, measuring 6. 003 km and ranking as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One racing. The circuit first hosted the European Grand Prix in 2016, before becoming the permanent home of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix starting in 2017, with operations managed by Baku City Circuit Operation Company.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km facility that hosted the Middle East's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix and continues to stage the annual F1 race alongside other motorsport events including GP2 racing and endurance competitions. The track, which holds FIA Grade 1 status, features multiple configuration options and has accommodated various racing series over the years.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657-kilometer circuit is renowned as a versatile motorsport venue featuring extended straights and diverse corner types suitable for comprehensive vehicle testing. The track holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Spa-Francorchamps is a 7. 004 km Belgian circuit nestled in the Wallonia region near the town of Spa, which has served as the home of the Formula One Belgian Grand Prix since 1925. The track gained further significance by hosting a race during the inaugural 1950 F1 season and has maintained an annual Grand Prix presence from 1985 onwards, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, this 4. 361 km circuit serves as the permanent home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the venue has hosted numerous international racing series including sportscar championships and North American racing competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, the Shanghai International Circuit is a motorsport venue renowned for hosting the Chinese Grand Prix, which took place annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The track additionally became home to the Shanghai ePrix starting in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near villages in Northamptonshire, England, Silverstone Circuit has been the primary venue for the British Grand Prix since becoming the championship's inaugural race in 1950. After sharing hosting duties with two other tracks between 1955 and 1986, the circuit became the permanent home of Britain's Formula One event from 1987 onwards.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: Located in Mogyoród near Budapest, the Hungaroring is a 4. 381 km circuit that hosted the inaugural Formula One Grand Prix in the Eastern Bloc when it opened in 1986, having been constructed in just eight months, making it the fastest-built track in the sport's history. The venue was established after Bernie Ecclestone pursued a race behind the Iron Curtain, with the Hungarian government opting to build a dedicated circuit outside the capital rather than a street course through Budapest's main park, and the opening race was dedicated to János Drapál, Hungary's pioneering motorcycle racing champion.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the 5. 793 km Autodromo Nazionale Monza is one of Europe's oldest purpose-built racing circuits, constructed in 1922 and renowned for its fast layout with extended straights and high-speed bends. The circuit has hosted the Italian Grand Prix annually since 1949, with only a single interruption in 1980 for renovation, making it one of Formula One's most consistently featured venues since the championship began.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km motorsport venue in Mie Prefecture, Japan, operated by Honda Mobilityland. The track hosts major international racing events, most notably the Formula One Japanese Grand Prix and the domestic Super Formula championship, with a spectator capacity of 155,000.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, weaving around the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its concentration of luxury hotels and casinos. The layout passes several iconic venues such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, making it one of motor racing's most visually distinctive urban venues.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is named after two Mexican racing brothers who died in separate incidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The circuit has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix since 2015 on its current layout, resuming the event after a 23-year absence from the calendar, though the race was previously held there on a different configuration until 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary street course constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners that produces average qualifying speeds near 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One use, the venue entered the championship calendar in 2022 as the Miami Grand Prix.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street track winding through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts of the Principality, skirting the harbour and earning its common reference as the "Monte Carlo" circuit due to its predominance within that particular neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Situated in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, the 4. 259 km Zandvoort circuit hosted the revived Dutch Grand Prix from 2021 until the partnership concluded in 2026. The track, renamed under sponsorship agreements, has been a significant venue for international motorsport racing in the Netherlands.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit sits north of Doha in Qatar and spans 5. 419 kilometres with a notably long main straight of 1. 068 kilometres.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Located in São Paulo, Brazil, Interlagos is a 4. 309 km counterclockwise circuit that opened in 1940 and was later renamed to commemorate the late Formula 1 driver José Carlos Pace, who tragically perished in an aircraft accident in 1977. The venue hosts major international racing events and features additional facilities including a karting track dedicated to another legendary Brazilian driver, Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: A street circuit situated along Jeddah's waterfront promenade beside the Red Sea, this venue has been home to the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since 2021. The track also began hosting a Formula E race in 2025, establishing itself as a key motorsport destination in the region.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's waterfront precinct, incorporating the urban areas of Downtown Core and Kallang into its layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced design with extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for comprehensive vehicle testing. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 track that serves as the home venue for the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside NASCAR and MotoGP racing. Beyond Formula One, the facility has hosted various motorsport series including endurance racing championships and previously featured IndyCar and rallycross competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British racing driver who represents Thailand in Formula One, currently driving for Williams.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Fernando Alonso, a Spanish driver currently racing for Aston Martin in Formula One, has secured two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006 while accumulating 32 Grand Prix victories throughout his 23-season career. Beyond Formula One, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans victories and a 2018-19 World Endurance Championship title, making him the sole driver to win both a Formula One world championship and a World Endurance championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli represents Mercedes in Formula One, having claimed seven race victories following his entry to the championship in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Haas, competing at the highest level of international motorsport.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One for Audi, bringing his competitive talent to the team's grid lineup.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One after a lengthy career spanning 13 seasons. He achieved two World Championship runner-up finishes during his time with Mercedes in 2019 and 2020, accumulating 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his racing career.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Colapinto is an Argentine motorsport competitor who currently races in Formula One with the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan currently holds a reserve role with Haas in Formula One while competing in European Le Mans Series prototypes with Nielsen Racing. He made seven Grand Prix appearances between 2024 and 2025.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: French driver Pierre Gasly currently races for Alpine in Formula One, having previously secured a victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar represents France in Formula One competition, driving for Red Bull Racing. The driver holds dual French and Algerian nationality.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently competing for Ferrari who has secured seven World Drivers' Championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record. He also holds multiple racing records including the most career victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: Nicolas Hülkenberg is a German driver currently competing in Formula One for Audi, bringing extensive experience from his long career in the sport. Beyond his Formula One commitments, he achieved a significant victory in endurance racing, winning the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand motorsport competitor currently driving for Racing Bulls in the Formula One championship.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc represents Monaco in Formula One racing with Ferrari, where he achieved second place in the 2022 drivers' championship. The Ferrari driver has secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine seasons in the sport.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish motorsport driver who competed in Formula One across two separate periods, from 2014-2020 and again from 2022-2024. Currently, he competes in the World Endurance Championship as a factory BMW driver for WRT, while also taking part in NASCAR's Cup Series with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris is a British Formula One driver competing for McLaren who secured the 2025 drivers' championship with the team. Across his eight seasons in the sport, he has claimed victory in 13 Grand Prix races.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon, a French racing driver, currently competes in Formula One for Haas. He achieved his sole Grand Prix victory during the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio Pérez, a Mexican driver, currently races for Cadillac in Formula One. The veteran competitor finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull and has claimed six Grand Prix victories throughout his 15-year career in the sport.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver competing for McLaren in Formula One, has achieved nine Grand Prix victories over the course of four seasons.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo is an Australian driver who spent 14 seasons racing in Formula One between 2011 and 2024, earning eight Grand Prix victories during his career. Known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," Ricciardo has since retired from the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell competes in Formula One for Mercedes, having secured seven Grand Prix victories during his eight-year tenure in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz has established himself as a Formula One competitor across more than a decade of racing, securing four Grand Prix victories during his career. He currently races for Williams in the championship.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver currently racing in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously driven LMP2 machinery in IMSA competition. His Formula One career spanned the 2023 and 2024 seasons.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian driver currently racing for Aston Martin in Formula One.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, held a full-time Formula One seat from 2021 through 2025 before transitioning to a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch-Belgian driver Max Verstappen represents the Netherlands in Formula One and races for Red Bull Racing. He has secured four consecutive world championship titles between 2021 and 2024, alongside 71 Grand Prix victories accumulated over his 12-season career.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu represents China as the sole Chinese driver to have competed in Formula One, having raced in the sport from 2022 through 2024. He currently holds a reserve driver position with the Cadillac Formula One team.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based squad rebranded as Alpine for the 2021 season, continuing Renault's factory involvement in Formula One under the French manufacturer's sports car marque. Operating as Alpine until Renault's departure at the conclusion of 2025, the team maintained its status as Renault's official works outfit throughout this period.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has entered Formula One through multiple iterations, with its current manifestation operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Racing banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of Italian luxury automaker Ferrari, is Formula One's oldest and most accomplished team, participating continuously since the championship's inaugural 1950 season. The squad, nicknamed after their distinctive equine emblem, has maintained an unbroken presence throughout the sport's entire history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: American team owner Gene Haas founded this F1 outfit in 2014, entering the championship for the first time in 2016. Under current team principal Ayao Komatsu, who took over from Guenther Steiner in early 2024, the squad competes as a U. S.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: This Swiss racing enterprise, established in 1970 by Peter Sauber, built both sports and Formula One cars as an independent manufacturer. Before joining Formula One in 1993, the outfit achieved endurance racing success including Le Mans victory in 1989, then competed in F1 for over three decades until 2025, ranking among the championship's longest-serving constructors before being absorbed into Audi's F1 program.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its Woking facility, operating as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group under ownership of Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has been a significant presence in Formula One since 1954, operating as both team proprietor and engine supplier across multiple eras. The current Mercedes-AMG Petronas operation, headquartered in Brackley and racing under a German licence, became a tripartite venture in January 2022 when Ineos acquired an equal ownership share alongside Mercedes-Benz Group and Toto Wolff. The team is traditionally known by the "Silver Arrows" epithet.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that commenced competition in 2024 as part of Red Bull's multi-team structure. Based in Faenza with additional facilities in Milton Keynes, the team operates as Red Bull's second racing outfit alongside the primary Red Bull Racing team.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as part of Red Bull's two-team operation. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility near Milton Keynes, the team functions as Red Bull Racing's sister squad within the Austrian conglomerate's racing portfolio.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licensed Formula One team established in 2005 and headquartered in England. Long under the stewardship of Christian Horner until his 2025 departure, the team is part of Red Bull GmbH's two-team racing portfolio, with the other being Racing Bulls.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's earlier failed racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in 2026 as Atlassian Williams F1 Team and operates from a substantial 60-acre facility.
